The Reality

The law is already in effect.
Most companies just don't know it yet.

SB 253 and SB 261 create mandatory climate disclosure requirements for companies doing business in California — with real deadlines, real penalties, and a state that isn't reliably telling companies they're covered.

01

You may already be in scope

SB 253 applies at $1B+ revenue, SB 261 at $500M+ — measured as the lesser of your last two fiscal years, not just the current one. California's own outreach to qualifying companies has been unreliable, so many affected companies don't yet know they're covered.

02

The deadline is closer than it looks

SB 253's first Scope 1 and 2 disclosures are due November 10, 2026. Non-compliance penalties run up to $500,000 per year and accrue daily — on top of CARB's own annual filing fee.

03

Scope 3 is coming, and it's not simple

CARB has proposed five mandatory Scope 3 categories starting in 2027. The requirements are still being finalized — the smart move is building flexible reporting infrastructure now, not scrambling to assemble it later.
